findings.highlight: I went to bed too to relieve Saber
findings.evidenceJa: 床についた
findings.governingReading: He went to bed to reassure Saber and put her mind at ease.
findings.explanation: Relieve Saber is nonidiomatic and can imply removing her from duty rather than easing her concern.

findings.highlight: it was a big turning point
findings.evidenceJa: とんでもない分かれ道だった
findings.governingReading: It was an extraordinary fork between two entirely different lives.
findings.explanation: Turning point removes the two-way path between the Emiya home and church custody.

findings.highlight: go through the heavy doors
findings.evidenceJa: 重苦しい扉に手をかけた
findings.governingReading: He places his hand on the oppressive door.
findings.explanation: The English advances Shirou through the doorway before the next scene and removes the hesitant physical threshold.

findings.highlight: I feel more afraid than I would in complete darkness
findings.evidenceJa: 下手な暗闇より緊張する
findings.governingReading: The vast illuminated silence makes him more tense than ordinary darkness would.
findings.explanation: Afraid changes bodily alertness and unease into explicit fear.

findings.highlight: Kotomine says so
findings.evidenceJa: 言峰はつまらなげに言って
findings.governingReading: Kotomine says it with evident boredom.
findings.explanation: The English removes Kotomine’s dismissive lack of interest from his first response.

findings.highlight: a park and passageway
findings.evidenceJa: 立派な庭園と渡り廊下
findings.governingReading: an impressive garden and covered connecting corridor
findings.explanation: Park changes the church’s designed inner garden into a public-land category.

findings.highlight: This inelegant room seems to be Kotomine’s.
findings.evidenceJa: 言峰神父の私室らしい
findings.governingReading: This appears to be Father Kotomine’s private room.
findings.explanation: The English omits that the austere stone space is his personal quarters.

findings.highlight: I am unfortunately out of alcohol.
findings.evidenceJa: 持てなす物のひとつもないが、許せ
findings.governingReading: He apologizes that he has nothing with which to receive or entertain his guest.
findings.explanation: mirror moon’s conditional alternate invents a specific lack of alcohol absent from the bound Japanese.

findings.highlight: Kotomine says so while sitting down.
findings.evidenceJa: ずっしりとソファーに身を預けながら
findings.governingReading: Kotomine settles his full weight heavily into the sofa as he speaks.
findings.explanation: Sitting down removes the weight and bodily ease of Kotomine’s posture opposite tense Shirou.

findings.highlight: As expected, I hate this guy.
findings.evidenceJa: やはりこの男は苦手だ
findings.governingReading: As expected, Shirou finds this man difficult to deal with.
findings.explanation: Hate overstates 苦手 and simplifies Shirou’s intimidated discomfort into hostility.

findings.highlight: Maybe Saber is a failure
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーは故障しているのか
findings.governingReading: Perhaps Saber is malfunctioning or damaged.
findings.explanation: Failure changes a conjecture about her abnormal functioning into a categorical judgment of her worth or status.

findings.highlight: All they have are memories from when they were alive.
findings.evidenceJa: 奴らにあるものは生前の記録だけだ
findings.governingReading: All Heroic Spirits possess is the record of their lives before death.
findings.explanation: Memories collapses Kotomine’s deliberate distinction between fixed biographical records and memories acquired after becoming a Heroic Spirit.

findings.highlight: The priest ponders as he must not assent to the fact.
findings.evidenceJa: 納得がいかないのか、神父は思案している
findings.governingReading: The priest ponders, apparently unable to make the account cohere.
findings.explanation: The English is grammatically malformed and turns observed lack of satisfaction into refusal to assent to a fact.

findings.highlight: She still hasn’t completed the contract to become a heroic spirit.
findings.evidenceJa: まだ英霊になる契約をしていない
findings.governingReading: Shirou says she has not yet made the contract to become a Heroic Spirit.
findings.explanation: The English silently repairs Shirou’s internally rough summary by changing whether the contract was made into whether it was completed.

findings.highlight: become a complete Servant
findings.evidenceJa: 英霊になる
findings.governingReading: become a complete Heroic Spirit, read as “Servant”
findings.explanation: The English retains only the ruby term and removes the Heroic Spirit/Servant layering from Shirou’s account.

findings.highlight: she continues to be summoned as a heroic spirit until she obtains the Holy Grail
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯を手に入れるまでは英霊として駆り出される
findings.governingReading: Until she obtains the Grail, she is repeatedly pressed into service as a Heroic Spirit.
findings.explanation: Neutral summoning removes the compulsory service expressed by 駆り出される and weakens the burden placed on Saber.

findings.highlight: she returns to her deathbed every time she fails
findings.evidenceJa: 死の直前にいる自身に戻ってしまう
findings.governingReading: Each failure returns her to her own self at the moment immediately before death.
findings.explanation: Deathbed invents a bed and replaces the temporal state with a concrete location that does not fit Saber’s death on the hill.

findings.highlight: all that is left for her is to be summoned as a Servant
findings.evidenceJa: 待っているのはサーヴァントとして使役される事だけ
findings.governingReading: All that awaits her is being made to serve as a Servant.
findings.explanation: The English again replaces compulsory use with the neutral event of being summoned, softening Kotomine’s bleak conclusion.

findings.highlight: a contradictory hero like Saber
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーみたいに矛盾した英霊
findings.governingReading: a contradictory Heroic Spirit like Saber
findings.explanation: Hero removes the defined supernatural category whose apparent contradiction Shirou is asking Kotomine to explain.

findings.highlight: Only the deviser would know about this.
findings.evidenceJa: 立案者であった当時の人間しか知るまい
findings.governingReading: Only the people of that era who devised it would know.
findings.explanation: The English changes a historical group of human planners into a single inventor.

findings.highlight: that is just the past
findings.evidenceJa: 元々はそういうモノだっただけ
findings.governingReading: That was simply what the system originally was or was based on.
findings.explanation: Just the past discards the claim about original nature and leaves Kotomine’s retraction nearly meaningless.

findings.highlight: for her to be summoned as the hero King Arthur
findings.evidenceJa: アーサー王という英雄として、彼女が使役される
findings.governingReading: for her still to be made to serve as the hero King Arthur
findings.explanation: A third neutral summons replaces forced service, weakening precisely what Shirou calls terribly wrong.

findings.highlight: Since Saber is still in the loop of time, she cannot be in two chances to obtain the Holy Grail at once
findings.evidenceJa: 未だ時間軸に留まっている為、“聖杯を手に入れる機会”を同時に行えるという訳でもない
findings.governingReading: Because Saber remains on the timeline, she cannot undergo multiple opportunities to obtain the Grail simultaneously.
findings.explanation: Loop adds cyclic mechanics, two invents a fixed number, and be in two chances is malformed English that obscures the constraint.

findings.highlight: If she continues to challenge each one
findings.evidenceJa: その全てを虱潰しに続けていけば
findings.governingReading: If she keeps working through every one of them exhaustively, one by one.
findings.explanation: The English loses 虱潰し, the systematic exhaustive-search logic supporting Kotomine’s claim that success is eventually inevitable.

findings.highlight: she’ll continue like this
findings.evidenceJa: あいつは一生あのままなんだ
findings.governingReading: She will remain that way for her entire life.
findings.explanation: The English removes the lifetime scope of Shirou’s conclusion and weakens its finality.

findings.highlight: be sent out to many ages
findings.evidenceJa: あらゆる時代に駆り出される
findings.governingReading: be pressed into service in every era
findings.explanation: Many narrows あらゆる from all eras, reducing the total scope of the fate Shirou imagines for Saber.

findings.highlight: she will return once she dies
findings.evidenceJa: 死んでしまえば死の直前にいる彼女に戻る
findings.governingReading: If that incarnation dies, she returns to herself at the moment just before her original death.
findings.explanation: The English omits the destination and therefore the central limit on keeping Saber alive in the present world.

findings.highlight: The heroic spirits and Servants are spurious.
findings.evidenceJa: 英霊とサーヴァントは似て非なるモノ
findings.governingReading: Heroic Spirits and Servants are similar in appearance or relation but fundamentally different things.
findings.explanation: Spurious means false or inauthentic and does not express the contrast between surface similarity and categorical difference.

findings.highlight: does not have a mind
findings.evidenceJa: 意思などない
findings.governingReading: Ordinarily summoned Heroic Spirits possess no will of their own.
findings.explanation: No mind broadens lack of volition into absence of mentality, changing Kotomine’s explanation of tool-like agency.

findings.highlight: a donor called the Holy Grail
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯という強大な魔力提供源
findings.governingReading: the Grail as an immense source supplying magical energy
findings.explanation: Donor personifies and obscures the Grail’s technical role as a power source supplementing the Master.

findings.highlight: He must have predicted my response.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の反発など予測していたのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou wonders whether Kotomine had anticipated even his resistance.
findings.explanation: The English promotes Shirou’s suspicious question into a confident factual conclusion.

findings.highlight: he was waiting to reach this conclusion from the beginning
findings.evidenceJa: 初めからこの結論に達したかった
findings.governingReading: His eyes seemed to say that this was the conclusion he had wanted to reach from the start.
findings.explanation: Waiting removes Kotomine’s purposive desire and makes the progression passive, weakening Shirou’s perception that he engineered the exchange.

findings.highlight: they have become a familiar summoned in this age
findings.evidenceJa: この時代の使い魔として立場を確立したにすぎぬ
findings.governingReading: They have merely established a stable position in this era as a familiar.
findings.explanation: The English replaces establishment of status with another act of summoning and obscures what drinking the Grail’s contents changes.

findings.highlight: This [r]ridiculous fight is pointless.
findings.evidenceJa: こんな馬鹿げた殺し合いは無意味だ
findings.governingReading: This ridiculous mutual killing is meaningless.
findings.explanation: A raw [r] control tag appears inside the English sentence, visibly interrupting the line; fight also weakens 殺し合い, though the finding is limited to the presentation defect.

findings.highlight: I want to end this fight and give it to Saber
findings.evidenceJa: 出来るのなら、セイバーに聖杯を渡してやる
findings.governingReading: He will end the fighting and, if it can be done, give the Grail to Saber.
findings.explanation: Omitting if possible turns a qualified hope into an unqualified intention and smooths over Shirou’s uncertainty about whether his plan can work.

findings.highlight: his words make my body shake so much that I want to vomit
findings.evidenceJa: 胸の中のモノを吐き出しそうなほど、体が震えてしまう
findings.governingReading: His body shakes as though everything inside his chest might come spilling out.
findings.explanation: The English converts a violent metaphor of inner exposure into a desire to vomit, flattening Shirou’s psychological reaction before the text separately names nausea.

findings.highlight: Just making the vessel is.
findings.evidenceJa: 器を作るだけならば、な
findings.governingReading: That is true if one is only making the vessel.
findings.explanation: The English is not a complete grammatical proposition and obscures Kotomine’s qualification.

findings.highlight: an omnipotent vessel
findings.evidenceJa: 願いを叶える“万能の釜”
findings.governingReading: the “omnipotent cauldron” that grants wishes
findings.explanation: Vessel erases the cauldron image just when Kotomine distinguishes the mythic prototype from the manufactured Grail vessel.

findings.highlight: this omnipotent vessel
findings.evidenceJa: あらゆる神話の根底にある“万能の釜”
findings.governingReading: the “omnipotent cauldron” said to lie at the foundation of every mythology
findings.explanation: The English deletes Kotomine’s sweeping claim that this motif underlies all mythologies.

findings.highlight: summoned the omnipotent vessel to the artificial Holy Grail
findings.evidenceJa: 人工物に過ぎない聖杯に“万能の釜”を降霊させ
findings.governingReading: invoke the “omnipotent cauldron” into the merely artificial Grail as a descended spirit
findings.explanation: The English treats the prototype as an object summoned to another object and loses the possession or spiritual-invocation mechanism.

findings.highlight: the golden rule of the line
findings.evidenceJa: ラインの黄金とやらの伝承
findings.governingReading: the tradition or legend of the Rhinegold
findings.explanation: mirror moon turns the Rhinegold proper name into the unrelated phrase “golden rule of the line.”

findings.highlight: They were the best suited to make an imitation of the Holy Grail.
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯の模造品を作る技術は神業だった
findings.governingReading: Their technique for making imitation Grails was virtually divine craftsmanship.
findings.explanation: Best suited changes an extraordinary level of technical accomplishment into comparative fitness for a task.

findings.highlight: the Church and the Magic Association were in the middle of a bloody war
findings.evidenceJa: 教会と魔術協会は係争の真っ最中だった
findings.governingReading: the Church and the Mages Association were in the midst of an active dispute or conflict
findings.explanation: Bloody war adds bloodshed and full-scale warfare that Kotomine does not state.

findings.highlight: A far eastern land was chosen as the place for the ritual.
findings.evidenceJa: 儀式には教会の目が届かない極東の地が選ばれた
findings.governingReading: A Far Eastern land beyond the Church’s surveillance was chosen for the ritual.
findings.explanation: The English omits the reason Fuyuki was selected: it lay beyond the Church’s watch.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka was in charge of the land around here
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂はここ一帯の霊地の持ち主
findings.governingReading: Tohsaka owned the spiritual land throughout this area.
findings.explanation: Being in charge replaces ownership of spiritual land with vague administrative responsibility.

findings.highlight: their master was a master of summoning
findings.evidenceJa: その師は降霊術の大家だった
findings.governingReading: their teacher was a great authority on spirit evocation
findings.explanation: Generic summoning loses the specific discipline and repeats “master” in two incompatible senses.

findings.highlight: three should be involved
findings.evidenceJa: 事は三すくみにすべきだ
findings.governingReading: the arrangement should be made a three-way deadlock
findings.explanation: The English preserves the number but removes the mutually checking power structure that motivates adding Makiri.

findings.highlight: a family with history
findings.evidenceJa: 長い年月を持つ名門
findings.governingReading: a distinguished lineage of long standing
findings.explanation: The English weakens both the depth of the lineage and its elite standing.

findings.highlight: ended while they were busy  killing each other.  fighting.
findings.evidenceJa: 連中が戦っている間に終わってしまった
findings.governingReading: It ended while the three families were fighting one another.
findings.explanation: Two competing phrasings survive in the active English line, exposing revision debris and making the sentence unreadable as published prose.

findings.highlight: the system to model the Servants
findings.evidenceJa: サーヴァントを形作るシステム
findings.governingReading: the system that forms or materializes Servants
findings.explanation: Model suggests representation or design rather than the system that gives Servants form.

findings.highlight: Illya’s family was the original proposer
findings.evidenceJa: その発案者がイリヤや遠坂の家だった
findings.governingReading: the families of Illya and Tohsaka were among those who originated the ritual
findings.explanation: The English drops Tohsaka and changes multiple founding houses into the Einzbern family alone.

findings.highlight: I don’t think she had anything with her
findings.evidenceJa: そんな荷物はなかった筈
findings.governingReading: She should not have had any such piece of luggage with her.
findings.explanation: Anything generalizes Shirou’s comic literal reading of “has the Grail” as a physical object or piece of baggage.

findings.highlight: It must have been a surprise.
findings.evidenceJa: よほど意外だったのか
findings.governingReading: Perhaps it was profoundly unexpected even to him.
findings.explanation: The English promotes Shirou’s reading of Kotomine’s reaction into certainty.

findings.highlight: A magus who knew about the Holy Grail War but did not become a Master.
findings.evidenceJa: マスターの資格を持ち得なかった魔術師
findings.governingReading: a magus who knew of the Grail War but could not possess the qualifications to be a Master
findings.explanation: The English changes inability to qualify into the historical fact of not becoming a Master, removing the eligibility constraint.

findings.highlight: Kotomine must be satisfied
findings.evidenceJa: 納得がいったのか
findings.governingReading: Apparently having reached an explanation—or perhaps satisfied with it—Kotomine rises.
findings.explanation: The English makes Shirou’s tentative reading of Kotomine’s behavior certain.

findings.highlight: The priest asks as if confirming it.
findings.evidenceJa: そんな言葉が投げられた
findings.governingReading: The words are thrown after Shirou’s retreating back, as though to confirm his understanding.
findings.explanation: The English removes the aggressive spatial image of Kotomine throwing the warning at Shirou’s back.

findings.highlight: What’s wrong?
findings.evidenceJa: どういう風の吹き回しだ
findings.governingReading: What brought on this uncharacteristic change of behavior?
findings.explanation: What’s wrong turns Shirou’s suspicion about Kotomine’s surprising advice into a generic inquiry about a problem.

findings.highlight: If you want to keep Saber
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーを存命させたいのなら
findings.governingReading: If you want to keep Saber alive
findings.explanation: The English omits alive, making Kotomine’s soul-feeding proposal sound like general possession or retention rather than continued life.

findings.highlight: He must not even care about my glare
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の凝視など堪えていないのか
findings.governingReading: As though Shirou’s fixed glare has no effect on him.
findings.explanation: The English makes Shirou’s inference about Kotomine’s response a certainty.

findings.highlight: the priest is laughing
findings.evidenceJa: 神父は愉快そうに笑っていた
findings.governingReading: the priest laughs as though thoroughly amused
findings.explanation: The English deletes Kotomine’s visible enjoyment of Shirou’s moral revulsion.

findings.highlight: did I offend you?
findings.evidenceJa: 失言だったか
findings.governingReading: Was that a slip of the tongue?
findings.explanation: Kotomine’s feigned admission that he misspoke becomes a question about Shirou taking offense.

findings.highlight: We have no right to say anything about it.
findings.evidenceJa: 我々が口を出す権利はない
findings.governingReading: We have no right to interfere in or dictate her life.
findings.explanation: Say anything broadens the prohibition and loses the specific sense of meddling in Saber’s decision.

findings.highlight: I shall investigate that Servant tomorrow.
findings.evidenceJa: 明日中に調べ上げよう
findings.governingReading: I will finish investigating that Servant by the end of tomorrow.
findings.explanation: Tomorrow removes both the completion encoded by 調べ上げる and the deadline encoded by 中に.

findings.highlight: Looking up at the  towering church, I leave this place.  church, I grit my teeth telling myself that I will never come here again.
findings.evidenceJa: 聳える伽藍を見上げながら、教会を後にした
findings.governingReading: Looking up at the towering church building, Shirou leaves the church.
findings.explanation: The active English contains two colliding exit variants and invents teeth-gritting plus a vow never to return, directly contradicting Kotomine’s invitation to return after the investigation.
